themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints surged to 3 THIS WEEK, up 1100% from the 0.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35), signaling a potential widespread tree health crisis or storm damage in Washington Heights/Inwood that demands immediate environmental assessment.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Aligns with community board's recurring request to 'Enhance park safety and reconstruct/upgrade parks and amenities'
reporting_angles: Did recent weather events (storms, extreme heat) trigger tree die-off across parks and streets?
Interview Parks Department about tree inspection protocols and maintenance backlog in CD112

themes_detail.label: Encampment Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 11 LAST WEEK, up 1000% from the 1.0-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.03), indicating a rapid emergence or visibility shift in homelessness/street living conditions across the neighborhood.
evidence: 11 encampment complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Community board has requested enhanced park safety (police/parks enforcement) as recurring priority, suggesting underlying concern
reporting_angles: Map encampment locations; interview residents and business owners about visible changes in past 1-2 weeks
Contact DHS, NYPD Homeless Outreach, and Parks Enforcement to understand if new encampments have formed or existing ones expanded

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints climbed to 5 LAST WEEK, up 264% from the 1.4-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.49), suggesting rapid proliferation of retail cannabis operations or community backlash against existing storefronts in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 5 cannabis retailer complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
No ULURP/zoning changes or new development permits filed that would explain surge; suggests unlicensed or unregulated operations
reporting_angles: Are new licensed retailers opening rapidly, or are residents complaining about unlicensed/illegal cannabis shops?
Interview NYPD Cannabis Enforcement Unit and NYC Department of Cannabis Management about enforcement activity in CD112

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Emergencies
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 2300% from the 0.1-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69), indicating serious blight or illegal dumping/abandonment affecting public spaces.
evidence: 3 lot condition complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
2300% spike with z-score of 8.69 (highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Community board has requested increased litter collection and park upgrades; suggests ongoing sanitation/blight concerns
reporting_angles: Identify which lots are driving complaints; visit sites to document conditions
Investigate if city has backlog in lot cleanup, or if illegal dumping has accelerated

themes_detail.label: Plumbing Complaints Decline
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints DROPPED 40% THIS WEEK to 62 complaints vs. the 102.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: -5.47), potentially indicating seasonal relief, successful city intervention, or a lag in complaint reporting that merits follow-up.
evidence: 62 plumbing complaints THIS WEEK vs. 102.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Plumbing remains #6 complaint category overall (1,187 complaints over 90 days), so improvement is noteworthy but may be temporary
reporting_angles: Did HPD or NYCHA complete a major repair program, or is this a data artifact/seasonal pattern?
Check if complaints are shifting to related categories (water leak, door/window) rather than truly declining
